problem.title_en: Existence of a 3-uniform 3-chromatic-critical hypergraph with minimum degree at least 7

posed.citation: P. Erdos, 3-critical 3-uniform hypergraphs (1974); erdosproblems.com/834; resolved by R. Li, arXiv:2512.24850 (2025)

recipients.contribution_en: Lean 4 formalization of the existence statement for a 3-uniform 3-chromatic-critical hypergraph on 9 vertices with 22 edges and minimum degree exactly 7, together with the edge-deletion and vertex-deletion certificates, the deletion-criticality conclusion and the exact minimum-degree conclusion.

problem.title_en: Vertex-count and edge-intersection restrictions in intersecting 3-chromatic uniform hypergraphs

posed.citation: P. Erdos and L. Lovasz, Problems and results on 3-chromatic hypergraphs (1975); erdosproblems.com/836

recipients.contribution_en: Lean 4 formalization of both finite-hypergraph answers: arbitrarily large active vertex counts refuting a uniform O(r^2) bound, and a linear bound forcing two distinct edges with r <= 2|E n F| + 1.

problem.title_en: Logarithmic lower bound for interpolation error amplification on every fixed subinterval

posed.citation: P. Erdos and P. Turan, An extremal problem in the theory of interpolation, Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1961) 221-234; erdosproblems.com/1153

recipients.contribution_en: Lean formalization submission for the frozen statement: for every fixed non-degenerate interval and every eps > 0, one threshold works for every sufficiently large node count and every choice of distinct nodes, giving (2/pi - eps) log n as a lower bound.

problem.title_en: Sifting half the residue classes modulo each of several primes while many integers survive

posed.citation: P. Erdos, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory (1980); erdosproblems.com/1202; Green's open problems, Problem 44

recipients.contribution_en: Separate AI-assisted Lean formalization contribution: a square-block construction producing, for every k and every lower bound N0, an N >= N0 with k increasing odd primes p_i satisfying p_i^10 < N^9 and exactly floor(p_i/2) forbidden residues each, while more than N/10 integers of [1,N] survive all sieves.
